llm.summary: This is a real n8n automation toolkit, but it needs Review because it can change live workflows and credentials while some install, transport, and persistence behaviors are under-scoped.

dimensions.detail: Network and credential use are proportionate for n8n administration, but authenticated n8n and Upstash requests allow cleartext HTTP/default redirects and some lack timeouts, which can expose API keys or leave operations indeterminate.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Install/update instructions use a mutable GitHub clone and git pull with broadly versioned Python dependencies; tidy-workflow can also npm-install a package into helpers/node_modules at runtime despite the package being described as read-only.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The trigger is very broad ('anything n8n-related'), several helpers mutate live n8n resources, and placeholder resolvers block absolute paths but not parent traversal, so user/workspace templates can inline files outside the workspace before deployment.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill creates persistent project guidance/memory files and may add CLAUDE.md/copilot instruction aliases; plugin docs also describe an automatic async PostToolUse tidy hook, but hook files were not present in the reviewed artifact.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The router, docs, and helpers coherently support n8n workflow authoring, deployment, debugging, credential linking/creation, Redis coordination, cloud-function scaffolding, and prompt iteration; these are high-impact capabilities but generally match the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you trust the publisher and are comfortable giving the harness n8n workflow/credential authority. Use HTTPS-only n8n and Upstash endpoints, prefer narrowly scoped API keys, pin to a reviewed commit or release, avoid plugin auto-hooks unless you want automatic template rewrites, and review templates for any ../ placeholder paths before deploying.
llm.findings:
[TT3] expected: The Upstash REST URL/token flow is expected for Redis queue cleanup, but the helper lacks HTTPS and redirect constraints, so the dataflow is a transport-risk concern rather than evidence of intentional exfiltration.
[TP4] expected: The flagged Redis cleanup, DSPy prompt iteration, UUID resolution, and cloud-function files are disclosed in the router/README as parts of the broader n8n harness, so the alleged purpose mismatch is downgraded.
[AE1] expected: The referenced Redis lock-pattern file is present locally and was inspected; this did not support an analysis-evasion finding.
[AR2] expected: The flagged 'no warning'/'no warnings' text appears in ordinary technical contexts, not as an instruction to suppress user-facing safety caveats.
[PE3] expected: Reading .env files is documented as subprocess-only credential handling for n8n/Redis operations; it is sensitive but purpose-aligned.
[TM1] expected: n8n variable deletion is documented and requires --force after a dry-run style preview, so it is a user-directed destructive operation, not hidden parameter abuse.
[SC4] unexpected: The lockfile does include form-data 4.0.4 under the helper npm dependency tree; this is a dependency hygiene issue to remediate, not malicious behavior by itself.
[SC6] expected: uvicorn is a legitimate FastAPI server dependency for the scaffolded cloud-function app; the typosquatting hypothesis was not supported by the artifact.
[AS1] expected: The artifact references ~/.claude/settings.json as manual hook configuration guidance, but inspected files did not show code that reads agent configuration directories.
[LP3] expected: Broad file, shell, environment, and network authority are expected for this harness, but the skill does not define tight allowed-tool boundaries for high-impact operations.
[SQP-1] expected: Routing all n8n-related requests to this skill is advertised, but broad routing increases the chance of invoking privileged helpers for loosely scoped requests.
[SQP-2] expected: Optional DSPy configuration uses external LLM providers and API keys; this is expected for prompt optimization but should be disclosed more clearly before prompts/datasets are sent out.
[T09] unexpected: Authenticated network access is expected, but allowing HTTP/default redirects and omitting timeouts on core clients is not proportionate for credential-bearing operations.
[T08] unexpected: Mutable clone/update instructions and unpinned dependency ranges create supply-chain drift outside the reviewed artifact.
